This refers to your 24 September 2012 letter requesting the Central Office's advice on who shall compose the Sangguniang Barangay of Timawa, Tanza Zone II, Iloilo City during the implementation of the Decision of the Office of the Ombudsman (Visayas) in OMB-V-A-II- 0569-H that meted the penalty of one (1) month and one (1) day suspension from service against the punong barangay, seven (7) councilors, the SK Chairman, Barangay Secretary and the Barangay Treasurer. You relate that prior to the issuance of the Ombudsman Decision suspending the entire membership of the sanggunian, one of the seven barangay councilors therein resigned and was immediately replaced through appointment by the Mayor. In view thereof, your Office now seeks the Central Office's guidance on the manner of filling the temporary vacancies caused by the suspension of the sangguniang barangay officials. We shall now proceed in our discussion on the manner of filling-up the temporary vacancies contemplated herein, namely: vacancy in the office of the punong barangay; vacancy in the office of the SK Chairman; and vacancies in the six (6) out of seven (7) seats of the regular sangguniang barangay members. Firstly, Section 46 of the Local Government Code (the "Code") governs the manner of filling-up a temporary vacancy in the office of the punong barangay for legal reasons, such as suspension from office, an in this case. Considering that only one (1) of the seven (7) councilors remains in office, he shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the punong barangay except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. This now leaves the entire seats of the regular members of the sanggunian vacant; the manner of filling the same shall be discussed lastly. Secondly, as regards the temporary vacancy in the office of the SK Chairman, the manner of filling-up the same is governed by the Section 4 (c), Article XVI of the 2001 Katipunan ng Kabataan and Sangguniang Kabataan Constitution and By-Laws, to wit: "Section 4. (c) In case of suspension of the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman, the successor, as determined in subsections (a) and (b) of this Section shall assume the position during the period of such suspension. " Section 4 (a) and (b) thereof provides as follows: t Section 4. (a) In case a Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, is convicted of a felony, voluntarily resigns, dies, is pennanently incapacitated, is removed from office, or has

been absent without leave for more than three (3) consecutive months as manifested in the records of the Sangguniang Barangay sessions or has been absent without valid reason for two (2) consecutive regular meetings of the Sangguniang Kabataan or for failure to call a regular meeting of the Sangguniang Kabataan and/or the Katipunan ng Kabataan, the Sangguniang Kabataan member who obtained the next higher number of votes in the election immediately preceding shall assume the office of the chairperson for the unexpired portion of the term, and shall discharge the powers and duties, and enjoy the rights and privileges appurtenant to the office. In case the said member refuses to assume the position or fails to qualify, the Sangguniang Kabataan member obtaining the next higher number of votes shall assume the position of the chairman for the unexpired portion of the term. (b) Where two (2) or more Sangguniang Kabataan members obtained the same next highest number of votes, the other Sangguniang Kabataan members shall conduct an election to choose the successor to the chairman from among the said members who obtained the same next highest number votes. " The SK Member who temporarily assumes the office of the SK Chairman during the latter's period of suspension shall assume the powers and duties of the SK Chairman, which includes the power and duty to sit as an ex-officio member of the sangguniang barangay. Lastly, as regards the manner of filling up the temporary vacancies in the seats of the seven (7) regular sangguniang barangay members, it may be observed that no such mechanism is provided by the Code. In our previously issued opinion denominated as DILG Opinion No. 39, s. 2006, we opined as follows: . the Local Government Code is silent on this mechanism as it merely provided for the filling up of permanent vacancies in the Sangguniang Panlungsod under Section 45 of the Local Government Code. This silence of the Code could have never been intended by Congress. Hence, it is incumbent upon the hierarchy in the Executive Branch, the local government units being part of the Executive Branch, to remedy this vacuum. Under Section 16, Article VII of the 1987 Constitution, it is provided that the President can appoint such officials whose manner of appointment is not provided for by law or is not vested with any appointing authority. To our mind, this is part of the residual power of the President. Accordingly, the remaining temporary vacant positions in the Sanggunian may be filled up by the President exercising her appointing authority by designating Officers-in-Charge/temporary members therein. .. who must possess all the qualifications of a candidate for local elective position under Section 39 of the Local Government Code, and none of the disqualifications under Section 40 of the same Code." In view of the foregoing considerations, it is our opinion that the temporary vacancies in the Sangguniang Barangay of Timawa, Tanza Zone II may be filled by the President of the Philippines as part of his residual power of appointment under Section 16, Article VII of the 1987 Constitution.

We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, J SUS Director 2—08 DO 1
